claim: The expression of the Notch ligand Dll4 fluctuates in individual endothelial cells within sprouting vessels in the mouse retina in vivo.
source: Here we show that the expression of the Notch ligand Dll4 fluctuates in individual endothelial cells within sprouting vessels in the mouse retina in vivo and in correlation with dynamic cell movement in mouse embryonic stem cell-derived sprouting assays.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental observations using Dll4 reporters in mouse retinas.

claim: Dll4 expression fluctuates in correlation with dynamic cell movement in mouse embryonic stem cell-derived sprouting assays.
source: Here we show that the expression of the Notch ligand Dll4 fluctuates in individual endothelial cells within sprouting vessels in the mouse retina in vivo and in correlation with dynamic cell movement in mouse embryonic stem cell-derived sprouting assays.
evidence: The abstract states this correlation, supported by time-lapse imaging data of embryoid body sprouting assays.

claim: Sprout elongation and branching associates with a highly differential phase pattern of Dll4 between endothelial cells.
source: We also find that sprout elongation and branching associates with a highly differential phase pattern of Dll4 between endothelial cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this association, which is demonstrated through imaging and quantification in the results.

claim: Stimulation with pathologically high levels of Vegf leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters in vitro.
source: Stimulation with pathologically high levels of Vegf, or overexpression of Dll4, leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data from cell culture and embryoid body assays with high Vegf treatment.

claim: Overexpression of Dll4 leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters in vitro.
source: Stimulation with pathologically high levels of Vegf, or overexpression of Dll4, leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experiments using ES cells with multiple copies of Dll4.

claim: Stimulation with pathologically high levels of Vegf leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters in vivo.
source: Stimulation with pathologically high levels of Vegf, or overexpression of Dll4, leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by in vivo experiments including Vegf injection into mouse retinas.

claim: Overexpression of Dll4 leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters in vivo.
source: Stimulation with pathologically high levels of Vegf, or overexpression of Dll4, leads to Notch dependent synchronization of Dll4 fluctuations within clusters, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by in vivo experiments using Dll4 reporter mice.

claim: The Vegf-Dll4/Notch feedback system normally operates to generate heterogeneity between endothelial cells driving branching.
source: Our results demonstrate that the Vegf-Dll4/Notch feedback system normally operates to generate heterogeneity between endothelial cells driving branching, whilst synchronization drives vessel expansion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conclusion, which is supported by experimental observations and computational modeling.

claim: Synchronization of the Vegf-Dll4/Notch feedback system drives vessel expansion.
source: Our results demonstrate that the Vegf-Dll4/Notch feedback system normally operates to generate heterogeneity between endothelial cells driving branching, whilst synchronization drives vessel expansion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conclusion, which is supported by experimental observations showing increased vessel diameter under conditions of synchronized Dll4 expression.

claim: A sensitive phase transition in the behaviour of the Vegf-Dll4/Notch feedback loop underlies the morphogen function of Vegfa in vascular patterning.
source: We propose that this sensitive phase transition in the behaviour of the Vegf-Dll4/Notch feedback loop underlies the morphogen function of Vegfa in vascular patterning.
evidence: The abstract proposes this mechanism based on the experimental findings and computational modeling results.

claim: Formation of a regularly branched blood vessel network is crucial in development and physiology.
source: The formation and maintenance of adequately branched and hierarchically organised networks of blood vessels is critical for all aspects of tissue growth and physiology (Potente et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Dll4/Notch signalling between activated endothelial cells functions to amplify stochastic differences in expression levels of Vegfr.
source: Recent work established that Dll4/Notch signalling between the activated endothelial cells functions to amplify stochastic differences in expression levels of the vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (Vegfr), ultimately establishing tip cells bearing high Vegfr expression, and inhibited stalk cells, bearing lower levels of signalling receptors (Jakobsson et al., 2010; Hellström et al., 2007; Suchting et al., 2007; Phng and Gerhardt, 2009; Lobov et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Dll4/Notch signalling establishes tip cells bearing high Vegfr expression and inhibited stalk cells bearing lower levels of signalling receptors.
source: Recent work established that Dll4/Notch signalling between the activated endothelial cells functions to amplify stochastic differences in expression levels of the vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (Vegfr), ultimately establishing tip cells bearing high Vegfr expression, and inhibited stalk cells, bearing lower levels of signalling receptors (Jakobsson et al., 2010; Hellström et al., 2007; Suchting et al., 2007; Phng and Gerhardt, 2009; Lobov et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The Dll4/Notch pathway establishes a lateral-inhibition feedback loop with the Vegf-Vegfr pathway.
source: The Dll4/Notch pathway thereby establishes a lateral-inhibition feedback loop with the Vegf-Vegfr pathway, controlling branching frequency by balancing the number of new tip cells with the number of stabilizing stalk cells (Phng and Gerhardt, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The Dll4/Notch pathway controls branching frequency by balancing the number of new tip cells with the number of stabilizing stalk cells.
source: The Dll4/Notch pathway thereby establishes a lateral-inhibition feedback loop with the Vegf-Vegfr pathway, controlling branching frequency by balancing the number of new tip cells with the number of stabilizing stalk cells (Phng and Gerhardt, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Tip and stalk cells regularly change position as endothelial cells dynamically compete for the tip position.
source: Genetic mosaic experiments in 3D embryoid body sprouting assays and in vivo illustrated tip and stalk cells regularly change position as endothelial cells dynamically compete for the tip position (Jakobsson et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Every 3–5 hr, the tip cell is exchanged, leading to continuously changing cellular neighbourhood relationships.
source: Every 3–5 hr, the tip cell is exchanged, leading to continuously changing cellular neighbourhood relationships.
evidence: This claim is stated as an established finding from previous work.

claim: Computational modelling illustrated that the Dll4/Notch-Vegf feedback loop should suffice to pattern new sprouts.
source: Computational modelling of the feedback loop illustrated that it should suffice to pattern new sprouts, and comprise a robust mechanism for the establishment of a regular branching pattern (Bentley et al., 2008; 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to computational modeling studies.

claim: The Dll4/Notch-Vegf feedback loop comprises a robust mechanism for the establishment of a regular branching pattern.
source: Computational modelling of the feedback loop illustrated that it should suffice to pattern new sprouts, and comprise a robust mechanism for the establishment of a regular branching pattern (Bentley et al., 2008; 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to computational modeling studies.

claim: The Notch/VEGF feedback drives differential VE-cadherin dynamics at individual endothelial junctions contributing to cell rearrangement behaviour.
source: Recently integrated modelling and experiments further identified that this Notch/VEGF feedback drives differential VE-cadherin dynamics at individual endothelial junctions contributing to cell rearrangement behaviour (Bentley et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to recent research.

claim: Notch signalling is highly dynamic in other cell systems.
source: In other cell systems, Notch signalling is highly dynamic, and Notch target genes oscillate both in single cells through autonomous feedback regulation, as well as in cell collectives (Masamizu et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Notch target genes oscillate both in single cells through autonomous feedback regulation and in cell collectives.
source: In other cell systems, Notch signalling is highly dynamic, and Notch target genes oscillate both in single cells through autonomous feedback regulation, as well as in cell collectives (Masamizu et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Notch activity synchronizes intrinsic oscillatory gene regulation between neighbouring mesoderm cells during somite formation.
source: The latter is best studied during formation of somites from the presomitic mesoderm, in which Notch activity synchronizes intrinsic oscillatory gene regulation between neighbouring mesoderm cells (Kageyama et al., 2007; Jiang, 2000; Hubaud and Pourquié, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research on somitogenesis.

claim: In the absence of Notch signalling, cells eventually drift out of synchrony, leading to loss of somite patterning.
source: In the absence of Notch signalling, cells eventually drift out of synchrony, finally leading to loss of somite patterning.
evidence: This claim is stated as an established finding from somitogenesis research.

claim: Dll4 over-expression in tumour cells in a glioblastoma model caused substantial vessel enlargement at the expense of branching.
source: Dll4 over-expression in tumour cells in a glioblastoma model caused substantial vessel enlargement at the expense of branching (Li et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Constitutive genetic endothelial activation of Notch4 leads to embryonic vessel diameter increase and arterio-venous shunt formation.
source: Constitutive genetic endothelial activation of Notch4 leads to embryonic vessel diameter increase and arterio-venous shunt formation, further suggesting that controlled Notch activity plays a role in vessel diameter regulation and adequate network remodelling (Uyttendaele et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Reduced Notch signalling in endothelial cells promotes a highly branched network with small calibre vessels.
source: Collectively, existing studies show that reduced Notch signalling in endothelial cells promotes a highly branched network with small calibre vessels whereas increased Notch activity promotes a sparse network of large calibre vessels.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Increased Notch activity promotes a sparse network of large calibre vessels.
source: Collectively, existing studies show that reduced Notch signalling in endothelial cells promotes a highly branched network with small calibre vessels whereas increased Notch activity promotes a sparse network of large calibre vessels.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Vegfa shows strong dosage dependent effects on vascular patterning.
source: Similarly, Vegfa shows strong dosage dependent effects on vascular patterning.
evidence: This claim is stated as an established observation in the field.

claim: Vegfa is genetically haplo-insufficient.
source: Like Dll4, Vegfa is genetically haplo-insufficient, and overexpression causes embryonic lethality (Miquerol et al., 2000; Carmeliet et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Vegfa overexpression causes embryonic lethality.
source: Like Dll4, Vegfa is genetically haplo-insufficient, and overexpression causes embryonic lethality (Miquerol et al., 2000; Carmeliet et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: High Vegfa consistently induced fluctuations with high amplitude and several peaks in dll4 mRNA levels in endothelial monolayers.
source: High Vegfa consistently induced fluctuations with high amplitude and several peaks (Figure 1f,i), which given the population based measurement indicates the cells are fluctuating in relative synchrony.
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1f and 1i.

claim: The dominant periodicity of dll4 mRNA fluctuations under high Vegf in endothelial monolayers was 5–6 hr.
source: Lomb-Scargle analysis (Dequéant et al., 2006) showed that the dominant periodicity in each dataset was 5–6 hr.
evidence: This claim is based on Lomb-Scargle analysis of the qPCR time course data.

claim: Under normal Vegfa levels, dll4 mRNA showed a low-amplitude rise and decline, but then remained relatively unchanged in endothelial monolayers.
source: Under normal Vegfa levels, dll4 mRNA showed an unexpected low-amplitude rise and decline, but then remained relatively unchanged (Figure 1e).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Simulation of the Vegf/Notch feedback in a 2D monolayer geometry revealed that cells fluctuate between salt-and-pepper pattern-like states and near-uniform Notch activation.
source: This model revealed that the restricted ability of cells to change shape in a monolayer (without filopodia extensions and Vegf gradients) destabilizes the salt and pepper pattern; they instead fluctuate between salt-and-pepper pattern-like states and then near-uniform Notch activation across the cells (Figure 1a,b and Video 1).
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling results shown in Figure 1a,b and Video 1.

claim: Simulation of higher levels of Vegfa in a monolayer model led to high amplitude, synchronized oscillations of Dll4.
source: Simulation of higher levels of Vegfa in this simple model led to high amplitude, synchronized oscillations of Dll4 (Figure 1c,d and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling results shown in Figure 1c,d and Video 2.

claim: The gamma-secretase inhibitor DAPT completely abolished the fluctuations of dll4 levels under high Vegfa in endothelial monolayers.
source: To confirm that the fluctuations observed in vitro are indeed Notch regulated, we utilized the gamma-secretase inhibitor DAPT, a potent inhibitor of Notch signalling (Hellström et al., 2007), which completely abolished the fluctuations of dll4 levels under high Vegfa (Figure 1g,h).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1g,h demonstrating the effect of DAPT treatment.

claim: The fluctuations of dll4 levels under high Vegfa require Notch activity.
source: Taken together these results suggest that high Vegfa levels synchronize contiguous endothelial cells in their fluctuating expression of Dll4, leading to dynamic and recurring fluctuations that require Notch activity.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the DAPT inhibition experiment showing that blocking Notch signaling abolishes the fluctuations.

claim: The Dll4-P2A-dVenus construct gave rise to viable and fertile mice.
source: Heterozygous knock-in ES cells and those carrying one distant copy of the Dll4-P2A-dVenus construct gave rise to high degree chimeras and germ line transmission, effectively establishing colonies of viable and fertile mice.
evidence: This claim describes the successful generation of mouse lines from the reporter construct.

claim: ES cells and mice carrying one additional copy of Dll4-P2A-dVenus showed 1.5 times the normal dll4 mRNA levels.
source: ES cells and mice carrying one additional copy showed expectedly 1.5 times the normal dll4 mRNA levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: dVenus protein expression and Dll4 protein expression showed perfect correlation in ES cells and mouse retinas.
source: Studying dVenus protein expression and Dll4 protein expression in ES cells and in mouse retinas from this strain showed perfect correlation between cells expressing dVenus and Dll4 protein (Figure 2a–d, g, h).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2a-d, g, h.

claim: dVenus has a half-life of 15 min.
source: Both reporters have a fast maturation time (Nagai et al., 2002; Day and Davidson, 2009); however, dVenus has an extremely short half-life (15 min), while Emerald has a half-life of 24–26 hr (Li, 1998; Corish and Tyler-Smith, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature on fluorescent protein properties.

claim: Emerald has a half-life of 24–26 hr.
source: Both reporters have a fast maturation time (Nagai et al., 2002; Day and Davidson, 2009); however, dVenus has an extremely short half-life (15 min), while Emerald has a half-life of 24–26 hr (Li, 1998; Corish and Tyler-Smith, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature on fluorescent protein properties.

claim: The distribution of dVenus showed the typical salt-and-pepper distribution pattern in embryoid bodies and postnatal mouse retina.
source: However, unlike dVenus, the distribution of Emerald protein was more widespread than Dll4 protein or dll4 mRNA. Both in the embryoid body ES cell sprouting assay (EB) (Jakobsson et al., 2007) and in the postnatal mouse retina, staining for dVenus showed the typical salt-and-pepper distribution pattern, with high levels in tip cells, and low levels in neighbouring stalk cells (Hellström et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence observations in embryoid bodies and retinas.

claim: Emerald protein was present at high levels in both Dll4 protein positive and Dll4 protein negative cells.
source: Emerald however was present at high levels in both Dll4 protein positive and Dll4 protein negative cells (Figure 2f), suggesting that Dll4 protein half-life is considerably shorter than that of Emerald.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: The salt-and-pepper distribution of dVenus and widespread distribution of Emerald provide evidence for dynamic phases of Dll4 expression in sprouting angiogenesis in vivo.
source: The salt-and-pepper distribution of dVenus and widespread distribution of Emerald provide the first evidence for dynamic phases of Dll4 expression in sprouting angiogenesis in vivo.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the differential distribution patterns of the two reporters with different half-lives.

claim: The salt-and-pepper distribution of Dll4 is not fixed, but dynamic.
source: Remarkably, these results indicate that the salt-and-pepper distribution is not fixed, but dynamic, consistent with the idea of continued and iterative competition for the tip position via Dll4/Notch signalling (Jakobsson et al., 2010).
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the differential distribution patterns of dVenus and Emerald reporters.

claim: High Vegfa conditions led to conspicuously short and stunted sprouts with much wider diameter in embryoid bodies.
source: However, high Vegfa conditions led to conspicuously short and stunted sprouts, with much wider diameter (Figure 3a).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological observations shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Under high Vegfa conditions, Dll4 and dVenus were expressed at very high levels in clusters of neighbouring cells close to the tip in embryoid bodies.
source: Interestingly, this morphological change from elongation to expansion invariably correlated with altered Dll4 and dVenus distribution. Although still most strongly expressed at the tip, Dll4 and dVenus were expressed at very high levels in clusters of neighbouring cells close to the tip (Figure 3b).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: High Vegfa levels disrupt the typical lateral-inhibition salt-and-pepper pattern and lead to more synchronized fluctuations of Dll4 levels in contiguous cells.
source: Thus, as predicted by computational modelling (Bentley et al., 2008; 2009) (Figure 1c), high Vegfa levels appear to disrupt the typical lateral-inhibition salt-and-pepper pattern and instead lead to more synchronized fluctuations of Dll4 levels in contiguous cells, thereby disrupting branching.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observed clustering of Dll4 expression under high Vegf conditions.

claim: 3Dll4-Emerald ES cells responded to high Vegfa with stunted sprouting, reduced branching and increased sprout diameter.
source: Also the 3Dll4-Emerald ES cells responded to high Vegfa with stunted sprouting, reduced branching and increased sprout diameter (Figure 3c).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological observations shown in Figure 3c.

claim: ES cells carrying multiple copies of the Dll4-dVenus transgene (7Dll4) showed high but dynamic levels of Dll4 expression, and synchronized in clusters of cells that correlated with stunted sprouting and vessel expansion.
source: Indeed, ES cells carrying multiple copies of the Dll4-dVenus transgene (7Dll4) showed high but dynamic levels of Dll4 expression, and synchronized in clusters of cells that correlated with stunted sprouting and vessel expansion (Figure 3 e-i).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations and quantifications shown in Figure 3e-i.

claim: DAPT treatment restored branching and elongation under high Vegfa or Dll4 overexpression conditions.
source: DAPT treatment restored branching and elongation under high Vegfa or Dll4 overexpression conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), demonstrating that this synchronization and morphogenesis effect is Notch mediated.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The synchronization and morphogenesis effect under high Vegfa or Dll4 overexpression is Notch mediated.
source: DAPT treatment restored branching and elongation under high Vegfa or Dll4 overexpression conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), demonstrating that this synchronization and morphogenesis effect is Notch mediated.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the rescue of normal phenotype by DAPT treatment.

claim: The temporal profiles of Dll4-dVenus intensity in individual spheres filling sprouts showed no synchrony between neighbouring cell fluctuations under normal conditions.
source: However, the profiles between the spheres filling the sprouts showed no synchrony between neighbouring cell fluctuations, in line with the salt-and-pepper distribution of Dll4 between neighbouring cells (Figure 4a–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data and quantification shown in Figure 4a-d.

claim: The asynchronous dynamic Dll4 expression behaviour correlated with a continuous forward movement of the leading tip in embryoid body sprouts.
source: The asynchronous dynamic Dll4 expression behaviour correlated with a continuous forward movement of the leading tip (Figure 4e–f, Figure 4—figure supplement 2a,b; Video 7, 10 and 11).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 4e-f and supplementary figures.

claim: In embryoid bodies overexpressing Dll4 (7Dll4 clone), the patterns of Dll4 expression between neighboring spheres appeared more synchronized.
source: However, collectively, the patterns of Dll4 expression between neighboring spheres appeared more synchronized (Figure 4i,j).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 4i,j.

claim: Wide sprouts in 7Dll4 embryoid bodies moved forward led by a cluster of several cells synchronously expressing high Dll4-dVenus levels.
source: Intriguingly, these wider sprouts moved forward led by a cluster of several cells synchronously expressing high Dll4-dVenus levels (Video 8, 12 and 13, Figure 4—figure supplement 2c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in videos and supplementary figures.

claim: High Vegfa levels induced clustering and iterative extension and retraction concomitant with synchronized dll4 reporter fluctuations at the tip in embryoid bodies.
source: Similarly, high Vegfa levels induced clustering and iterative extension and retraction concomitant with synchronized dll4 reporter fluctuations at the tip (Figure 4m–r, Video 9, 14 and 15, Figure 4—figure supplement 2e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 4m-r and videos.

claim: dVenus and dll4 mRNA expression showed a salt-and-pepper distribution in control retinas.
source: Fluorescent ISH allowed the detection of nascent dll4 mRNA (one or two dots) in the nucleus as well as mature mRNA in the cytoplasm of actively transcribing ECs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). dVenus and dll4 mRNA expression showed a salt-and-pepper distribution in control retinas, but strong clustering of dll4 positive cells in Vegfa injected retinas 20 hr post-injection (Figure 5a–h).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5a-h.

claim: Vegfa injection led to strong clustering of dll4 positive cells in retinas 20 hr post-injection.
source: dVenus and dll4 mRNA expression showed a salt-and-pepper distribution in control retinas, but strong clustering of dll4 positive cells in Vegfa injected retinas 20 hr post-injection (Figure 5a–h).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5a-h.

claim: Despite strong Vegfa stimulation, clusters of dll4 negative cells were present in Vegfa injected retinas.
source: Intriguingly, despite the strong Vegfa stimulation, clusters of dll4 negative cells were also present, arguing against a simple linear relationship between Vegf and Dll4 expression.
evidence: This observation is noted from the fluorescent in situ hybridization data.

claim: The change in spatial Dll4 expression distribution after Vegfa injection correlated with a dramatic shift from branching and extension to vessel enlargement.
source: The change in spatial Dll4 expression distribution correlated with a dramatic shift from branching and extension to vessel enlargement, remarkably similar to what we observed in the EB system (Figure 3).
evidence: This correlation is observed by comparing Dll4 expression patterns with vascular morphology.

claim: After Vegfa injection, most sprouts at the retinal sprouting front disappeared and were replaced by a dramatically widened peripheral vessel with occasional protrusions.
source: At the sprouting front, most of the sprouts had disappeared and were replaced by a dramatically widened peripheral vessel with occasional protrusions.
evidence: This morphological change is observed in retinas after Vegfa injection.

claim: After Vegfa injection, all vessels in the retinal plexus increased substantially in diameter while the overall branching frequency was significantly reduced.
source: In the plexus, all vessels increased substantially in diameter while the overall branching frequency was significantly reduced (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Radial expansion of the vascular plexus was significantly reduced after Vegfa injection.
source: Radial expansion of the vascular plexus was also significantly reduced, consistent with earlier reports (Gerhardt et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Computational simulations predicted that iterative synchronized sprouting and retraction generated by synchronized fluctuations in Notch signaling should lead to accumulation of empty collagen sleeves ahead of the vascular front.
source: Simulations of collagen matrix deposition of advancing sprouts in this model further predicted that the iterative synchronized sprouting and retraction movement generated by the synchronized fluctations in Notch signaling should lead to accumulation of empty collagen sleeves ahead of the vascular front (Figure 5i; Video 16).
evidence: This prediction is based on computational modeling shown in Figure 5i and Video 16.

claim: Retinas injected with Vegfa showed a dramatic mismatch between the vasculature and collagen IV deposition in the blunted regions of the sprouting front.
source: Testing this prediction, we assessed the pattern of collagen IV basement membrane deposition at the vascular sprouting front 3 hr (P4 retinas) and 20 hr (P5 retinas) after Vegfa injection. Retinas injected with Vegfa showed a dramatic mismatch between the vasculature and collagen IV deposition in the blunted regions of the sprouting front (Figure 5j,k).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5j,k.

claim: Collagen IV sleeves protruded ahead of the blunted vasculature 3 hr after Vegfa injection, and further increased in number and length over time.
source: In these areas, already 3 hr after Vegfa injection, collagen IV sleeves protruded ahead of the blunted vasculature, and further increased in number and length over time (Figure 5l–o).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5l-o.

claim: The observed radial expansion delay after Vegfa injection is likely a result of unproductive and iterative sprouting and retraction.
source: The observed radial expansion delay (Figure 5p) is thus likely a result of unproductive and iterative sprouting and retraction.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation of empty collagen sleeves and reduced radial expansion.

claim: Injecting Vegfa into the vitreous leads to widespread endothelial proliferation throughout the retinal plexus.
source: A plausible alternative explanation for the observed enlargement in vessel diameter upon high Vegfa levels is cell proliferation. Indeed, injecting Vegfa into the vitreous leads to widespread endothelial proliferation throughout the plexus (Figure 6a,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 6a,c.

claim: Mitomycin C treatment completely blocked proliferation in retinas after Vegfa injection.
source: To discriminate between proliferation and collective endothelial cell synchronization effects, we inhibited proliferation by systemic treatment with mitomycin C (MMC) 24 hr prior to and again concomitant with intraocular mVegfa 165 injection, and analysed proliferation and retinal patterning 24 hr post Vegfa treatment. EdU incorporation revealed a complete block in proliferation in the MMC treated samples (Figure 6a–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 6a-d.

claim: The diameter increase at expense of branching complexity after Vegfa treatment was equally evident in samples from MMC plus Vegfa treated pups.
source: Interestingly however, the diameter increase at expense of branching complexity after Vegfa treatment was equally evident in samples from MMC plus Vegfa treated pups (Figure 6k,l).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6k,l.

claim: The morphogenic effects of quantitative changes in Vegfa are independent of proliferation.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first direct evidence for the morphogenic effects of quantitative changes in Vegfa to be independent of proliferation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation that vessel diameter increase occurs even when proliferation is blocked.

claim: In 3Dll4-dVenus reporter mice, OIR leads to strong clustering of endothelial cells positive or negative for dVenus in the neovascular tufts.
source: In 3Dll4-dVenus reporter mice, OIR leads to strong clustering of endothelial cells positive or negative for dVenus in the neovascular tufts (Figure 7a–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7a-d.

claim: OIR leads to an overall increase in Dll4-dVenus levels.
source: Similar to Vegfa injection, OIR also leads to an overall increase in Dll4-dVenus levels (Figure 7a).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: dll4 mRNA and protein expression in WT retinas confirmed clustering of cells with high and low expression in OIR.
source: dll4 mRNA and protein expression in WT retinas confirmed clustering of cells with high and low expression, compatible with the idea of localized synchronization of endothelial Dll4 fluctuations in OIR (Figure 7e–h; Figure 5—figure supplement 2g–i).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7e-h and supplementary figures.

claim: Collagen IV deposition poorly matched the vasculature in OIR retinas, revealing that substantial extensions had previously formed beyond the sprouting front and tufts.
source: Collagen IV deposition poorly matched the vasculature, revealing that substantial extensions had previously formed beyond the sprouting front and tufts in the OIR retinas (Figure 7i–k).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7i-k.

claim: Glomeruloid tuft formation in OIR is associated with iterative extension and retraction of endothelial processes, which fail to establish functional new branches.
source: These results indicate that the glomeruloid tuft formation in OIR is associated with iterative extension and retraction of endothelial processes, which however fail to establish functional new branches.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation of empty collagen sleeves in OIR.

claim: In glioblastoma, some vessels showed little or no dll4 signal, while other vessels showed high levels of expression in all neighboring endothelial cells.
source: dll4 fluorescent ISH performed on 200 µm vibratome sections of GBM revealed a highly irregular pattern of expression (Figure 8a). Whilst some vessels showed little or no signal at all, other vessels showed high levels of expression in all neighboring endothelial cells (Figure 8 a–c).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 8a-c.

claim: Vessels close to the hypoxic core in glioblastoma generally exhibited the highest dll4 expression and strong clustering frequently associated with local vessel diameter increase.
source: Vessels close to the hypoxic core generally exhibited the highest expression and strong clustering frequently associated with local vessel diameter increase.
evidence: This observation is noted from the fluorescent in situ hybridization data in glioblastoma samples.

claim: Dll4 protein expression showed clustering of high levels in adjacent cells in glioblastoma.
source: Similarly Dll4 protein expression showed clustering of high levels in adjacent cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2j,k).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2j,k.

claim: The aberrant vascular patterning in GBM was associated with extensive empty collagen IV sleeves radiating from the tumour vessels.
source: Furthermore, the aberrant vascular patterning in GBM was associated with extensive empty collagen IV sleeves radiating from the tumour vessels (Figure 8d–f).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8d-f.

claim: Endothelial cell Dll4/Notch signalling and sprouting behaviour becomes locally synchronized between neighboring cells during tumour angiogenesis.
source: These results provide the first evidence for iterative sprouting and retraction and, together with the Dll4 expression pattern, indicate that endothelial cell Dll4/Notch signalling and sprouting behaviour becomes locally synchronized between neighboring cells during tumour angiogenesis.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation of clustered Dll4 expression and empty collagen sleeves in glioblastoma.

claim: The salt-and-pepper differential pattern of Dll4 expression normally associated with vascular branching switches to synchronized fluctuations under conditions of experimental high Vegfa, in retinopathy and tumour angiogenesis.
source: Together our results demonstrate that the salt-and-pepper differential pattern of Dll4 expression normally associated with vascular branching switches to synchronized fluctuations under conditions of experimental high Vegfa, in retinopathy and tumour angiogenesis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental findings across different models.

claim: Nonlinear synchronized fluctations in Dll4/Notch drive vessel expansion and disrupt effective cell rearrangement and migration leading to reduced branching and elongation.
source: Dynamic observations in the EB model suggest that nonlinear synchronized fluctations in Dll4/Notch drive vessel expansion and disrupt effective cell rearrangement and migration leading to reduced branching and elongation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on time-lapse imaging observations in embryoid bodies.

claim: Notch signalling activity between activated endothelial cells undergoes a phase transition between two distinct operational modes, depending on the levels of Vegfa.
source: Our current results provide evidence that Notch signalling activity, between activated endothelial cells, undergoes a phase transition between two distinct operational modes, depending on the levels of Vegfa.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental findings.

claim: At normal physiological levels of Vegfa, Dll4 fluctuates dynamically in individual cells and the lateral-inhibition feedback with the Vegfr system generates differences between neighbouring cells as a salt-and-pepper distribution.
source: At normal physiological levels, that typically correspond with developmental angiogenesis, Dll4 fluctuates dynamically in individual cells; the lateral-inhibition feedback with the Vegfr system functions to generate differences between neighbouring cells that manifest themselves as a salt-and-pepper distribution of Dll4 high and low cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings under normal Vegf conditions.

claim: The differential behaviour of tip and stalk cells is critical for branching and continuous elongation.
source: Dynamic observations in embryoid body sprouting assays indicate that the differential behaviour is critical for branching and continuous elongation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on time-lapse imaging observations in embryoid bodies.

claim: At higher Vegfa levels, the dynamic fluctuations between neighbouring cells become synchronized, corresponding with a loss of salt-and-pepper patterning.
source: At higher Vegfa levels however, the dynamic fluctuations between neighbouring cells become synchronized, corresponding with a loss of salt-and-pepper patterning.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings under high Vegf conditions.

claim: Synchronization of Dll4 levels is dependent on Notch activity.
source: This synchronization, and thus local clustering of cells with high or low Dll4 levels, is dependent on Notch activity, as dampening or inhibiting Notch activity disrupts synchronization.
evidence: This conclusion is based on DAPT inhibition experiments.

claim: Synchronization of Dll4 levels coincides with synchronized sprouting activity, disrupting sprouting and branching and causing vessel expansion.
source: Observations of dynamic behaviour in EBs stimulated with high Vegfa demonstrate that synchronization of Dll4 levels coincides with synchronized sprouting activity. As a consequence, sprouting and branching is disrupted and the vessel instead expands (Figure 9).
evidence: This conclusion is based on time-lapse imaging observations in embryoid bodies under high Vegf.

claim: Synchronization is an important principle of vessel malformation in disease.
source: The finding of clustered Dll4 expression by in situ hybridisation, Dll4 reporter and protein staining in the vessel expansions in the OIR model and in dilated vessels after Vegfa injection and in mouse glioblastomas together indicate that synchronization is an important principle of vessel malformation in disease.
evidence: This conclusion is based on observations across multiple disease models.

claim: Dll4 overexpression leads to synchronization and clustering and loss of branching even in the absence of altered Vegfa levels.
source: Dll4 overexpression, despite under the normal regulatory control, in the absence of altered Vegfa levels, also leads to the same synchronization and thus clustering and loss of branching.
evidence: This conclusion is based on experiments with ES cells carrying multiple copies of Dll4.

claim: Vegfa-induced Dll4 up-regulation is the key to synchronization.
source: Together with the observed up-regulation of Dll4 under Vegfa control, this suggests that Vegfa-induced Dll4 up-regulation is the key to synchronization.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both high Vegf and Dll4 overexpression lead to synchronization.

claim: Synchronization itself is the major driver of the switch from branching to expansion.
source: The observed clustering, stunted sprouting and expansion upon Dll4 overexpression in the absence of an altered Vegfa environment further suggests that synchronization itself is the major driver of the switch from branching to expansion.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the Dll4 overexpression experiments.

claim: Computational modelling predicted that reduced Vegfa gradients interfere with tip/stalk specification.
source: Computational modelling previously predicted that reduced Vegfa gradients interfere with tip/stalk specification as the reduced differences in the local environment make it more difficult for the lateral-inhibition feedback loop to establish differences between neighboring endothelial cells (Bentley et al., 2008; 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous computational modeling studies.

claim: A loss in Vegfa gradient pushes the system towards synchronization, an effect that is dramatically aggravated by higher Vegfa levels.
source: A loss in gradient already pushes the system towards synchronization, an effect that is dramatically aggravated by higher Vegfa levels.
evidence: This conclusion is based on computational modeling predictions and experimental observations.

claim: The underlying mechanism driving expansion and clustering in situations of reduced Vegfa gradients and high Vegfa levels lies in Dll4/Notch mediated synchronization of adjacent cells.
source: Our present findings indicate that the underlying mechanism driving expansion and clustering, instead of branching and elongation, in situations of reduced Vegfa gradients and high Vegfa levels lies in Dll4/Notch mediated synchronization of adjacent cells as they fail to establish a dynamic salt and pepper pattern.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings.

claim: Overexpression of Dll4 in tumour cells leads to reduced vessel branching and dramatically increased tumour vessel diameter.
source: Intriguingly, overexpression of Dll4 in tumour cells has been shown to lead to reduced vessel branching and dramatically increased tumour vessel diameter, with evidence that tumour cell Dll4 activates endothelial Notch receptors (Li et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Overexpression of Dll4 in tumour cells may cause synchronization of endothelial Notch dynamics, similar to overexpressed endothelial Dll4.
source: In the light of our current results it is tempting to speculate that overexpression of Dll4 in tumour cells adjacent to the endothelium will cause synchronization of endothelial Notch dynamics, similar to the situation of overexpressed endothelial Dll4.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the current findings.

claim: Inhibition of Dll4 by antibody, genetic haploinsufficiency or Notch inhibition by DAPT all lead to a dramatic increase in vessel branching, but reduced vessel diameter in tumour vessels.
source: Conversely, inhibition of Dll4 by antibody, genetic haploinsufficiency or Notch inhibition by DAPT all lead to a dramatic increase in vessel branching, but reduced vessel diameter in tumour vessels (Ridgway et al., 2006; Noguera-Troise et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The switch in tumour vessel patterning upon Dll4/Notch inhibition is driven by the loss of synchronization.
source: We propose that this switch in tumour vessel patterning is driven by the loss of synchronization, and thus a switch from collectively synchronized cell behaviour to differential individual behaviour.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the current findings.

claim: Synchronization leads to vessel expansion through the loss of adhesion differences.
source: Given our recent identification of Notch-regulated differential VE-cadherin adhesion (Bentley et al., 2014), it is conceivable that synchronization leads to vessel expansion through the loss of adhesion differences.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on recent findings about VE-cadherin dynamics.

claim: Differential adhesion drives intercalation and vessel elongation, whereas synchronization disrupts intercalation, causing cells to cluster and enlarge vessel diameter.
source: According to this concept, differential adhesion drives intercalation and thus vessel elongation, whereas synchronization disrupts intercalation, thus causing cells to cluster and thereby enlarge vessel diameter.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the current findings.

claim: Endothelial cell migration presents the key mechanism in vessel remodelling as opposed to endothelial cell apoptosis.
source: As endothelial cell migration as opposed to endothelial cell apoptosis appears to present the key mechanism in vessel remodelling (Franco et al., 2015), our current finding of Vegfa-induced vessel enlargement and loss of branching in the absence of proliferation further supports the idea that synchronization disrupts the normal differential migration/intercalation behaviour of endothelial cells and thereby leads to the observed morphological changes.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Notch inhibition is sufficient to break the synchronisation and restore branching morphogenesis in embryoid bodies overexpressing Dll4 or treated with high Vegfa levels.
source: Our observations in EBs overexpressing Dll4 or treated with high Vegfa levels demonstrate that Notch inhibition is sufficient to break the synchronisation and restore branching morphogenesis.
evidence: This conclusion is based on DAPT treatment experiments in embryoid bodies.

claim: The presomitic mesoderm close to the tip of the tail bud shows dynamic activity of Dll/Notch and Notch target genes of hes/hey family.
source: The presomitic mesoderm close to the tip of the tail bud shows dynamic activity of Dll/Notch and Notch target genes of hes/hey family.
evidence: This is stated as an established finding from somitogenesis research.

claim: The zone closest to the tip in presomitic mesoderm shows unsynchronized salt-and-pepper patterning of Dll/Notch activity, whilst temporal waves of synchronized activity emerge just rostral of this zone.
source: Intriguingly, the zone closest to the tip shows unsynchronized salt-and-pepper patterning of this activity, whilst temporal waves of synchronized activity emerge just rostral of this zone.
evidence: This is stated as an established finding from somitogenesis research.

claim: Dll/Notch activity between cells is the driver of synchronization in somitogenesis.
source: Although many genes and components of the Notch, Fgf and Wnt-signaling pathway oscillate in the presomitic mesoderm (Aulehla et al., 2008; Wahl et al., 2007; Goldbeter and Pourquié, 2008) and single cells oscillate autonomously through feedback loops in the regulation of the hes family of transcriptional repressors (Kageyama et al., 2007; Webb et al., 2016), it has become clear that Dll/Notch activity between the cells is the driver of synchronization.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on somitogenesis.

claim: In the absence of Notch activity or Dll expression, cells gradually drift out of synchrony in somitogenesis, leading to loss of somite pattern and vertebrae defects.
source: In the absence of Notch activity or Dll expression cells gradually drift out of synchrony, leading to loss of somite pattern and thus vertebrae defects.
evidence: This is stated as an established finding from somitogenesis research.

claim: The levels of Dll expression critically influence synchronization and affect the periodicity of the synchronized oscillations by changing the strength of coupling between neighbouring cells.
source: Recent work by Oates and colleagues using mathematical modelling and experimentation identified that the levels of Dll expression not only critically influence synchronization, but also affect the periodicity of the synchronized oscillations by changing the strength of coupling between the neighboring cells (Herrgen et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Rising Dll4 levels under the influence of Vegfa stimulation increase the coupling strength between neighbouring endothelial cells.
source: Thus, although the precise wiring of the signalling circuit is different, there is a striking analogy in that rising Dll4 levels under the influence of Vegfa stimulation will increase the coupling strength between neighbouring endothelial cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the analogy with somitogenesis and the experimental observations.

claim: Increased coupling strength between endothelial cells drives the cells to switch from differential to synchronized behaviour and to iterative sprouting and retraction, disrupting branching morphogenesis.
source: This will ultimately drive the cells to switch from differential to synchronized behaviour and thus to iterative sprouting and retraction, disrupting branching morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings and analogy with somitogenesis.

claim: The identified switch in behaviour from differential to synchronized by changing Dll4/Notch coupling strength identifies a novel mechanism of action for a morphogen.
source: Further, the identified switch in behaviour from differential to synchronized by changing Dll4/Notch coupling strength between endothelial cells under the influence of rising Vegfa concentrations identifies a novel, and to date unique, mechanism of action for a morphogen.
evidence: This is a proposed novel mechanism based on the current findings.

claim: The identified mechanism has wide reaching implications for understanding the effects of anti-Vegfa therapy in cancer.
source: From an applied perspective, the identified mechanism has wide reaching implications for our understanding of the effects of anti-Vegfa therapy in cancer, and will hopefully stimulate new research into dosing regimes of both Vegfa and Dll4/Notch inhibitors, separate and in combination, and effects on vessel normalization.
evidence: This is a speculation about the implications of the findings.
